skill.name: chrome-devtools-debugging
skill.description: Debug and analyze web applications using Chrome DevTools MCP. Use for console log inspection, network request monitoring, performance analysis, and debugging authenticated sessions. For basic browser automation (screenshots, form filling), use browser-discovery skill instead.
skill.summary: Debug web apps with Chrome DevTools MCP for console, network, performance, and authenticated browser analysis.
skill.author: Consiliency

security_audit.summary: Most static detections are markdown examples, placeholder URLs, or inline API names rather than malicious code. Real risks remain because the skill intentionally runs local commands, controls a Chrome DevTools session, evaluates browser JavaScript, and demonstrates printing authenticated tokens and cookies.

remediation.issue: Examples print authenticated storage, cookies, tokens, and request details.
remediation.suggestion: Replace full-value printing with redacted summaries and warn users before inspecting authenticated sessions.

remediation.issue: Chrome remote debugging is enabled on a fixed local port.
remediation.suggestion: Recommend a temporary test profile, loopback-only binding, and closing Chrome after debugging.

remediation.issue: The MCP server is referenced through npx with the latest tag.
remediation.suggestion: Pin a reviewed package version and require explicit user approval before running npx.

remediation.issue: The workflow executes local Python commands through Bash.
remediation.suggestion: Document that commands require user trust and must not include unreviewed user-controlled input.

static_findings.snippet: Look for: `Access to XMLHttpRequest... has been blocked by CORS policy`
For Chrome 145+, enable remote debugging at `chrome://inspect/#remote-debugging`.
- `select_page(page_idx, bring_to_front)` - Switch to tab by index
- `wait_for(text, timeout)` - Wait for text on page

semantic_findings.title: Authenticated Browser Data Exposure
semantic_findings.description: The skill demonstrates reading localStorage, sessionStorage, cookies, auth tokens, and request details from authenticated browser sessions. These examples can place credentials or personal data into assistant logs and transcripts.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Multiple documented examples explicitly print localStorage, sessionStorage, cookies, and token values from authenticated sessions. This is direct evidence of sensitive data exposure risk.

semantic_findings.title: Remote Debugging Endpoint Requires Isolation
semantic_findings.description: The setup instructs users to start Chrome with remote debugging on port 9222 and connect to that browser. A DevTools endpoint can control pages in the browser session, so it should be local, temporary, and isolated from normal browsing.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The setup instructions and reference both show connecting to Chrome remote debugging on 127.0.0.1:9222. This is expected for the skill but has clear browser-control impact if exposed or reused with a sensitive profile.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned MCP Server Execution
semantic_findings.description: The documentation references running chrome-devtools-mcp through npx with the latest tag. That can execute newly published npm package code without a pinned version or integrity review.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The npx command with the latest tag is present in both troubleshooting sections. The risk is supply-chain drift rather than evidence of malicious package behavior.

content.user_title: Debug Web Apps with Chrome DevTools
content.value_statement: Browser bugs often hide in console logs, network traffic, and authenticated state. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through Chrome DevTools MCP debugging.
actual_capabilities: Connects to Chrome DevTools MCP through documented Python wrappers.
Lists console errors, warnings, logs, and message details.
Inspects captured network requests, failed requests, headers, bodies, and timing.
Records performance traces and reviews available insight sets.
Evaluates JavaScript in the active browser context for debugging state.
Navigates pages and tabs during focused debugging sessions.
limitations: Requires Chrome DevTools MCP access and a running compatible browser.
Does not focus on screenshots, form filling, or broad browser automation.
Can expose cookies, tokens, and request bodies without careful redaction.
Examples assume the local Python wrapper path and environment are configured.

use_cases.title: Diagnose Frontend Console Failures
use_cases.description: Review browser errors, warnings, stack traces, and application state to identify likely frontend defects.

use_cases.title: Investigate Authenticated API Problems
use_cases.description: Inspect failed XHR and fetch requests after a manual login while protecting sensitive session data.

use_cases.title: Analyze Slow Page Loads
use_cases.description: Capture traces, find slow requests, and correlate performance issues with network and console evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect Console Errors
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner check of a loaded page.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Chrome DevTools debugging to list current console errors and warnings. Summarize likely causes and do not print secrets.

prompt_templates.title: Review Failed API Calls
prompt_templates.prompt: List recent failed XHR and fetch requests. Group them by status code, endpoint pattern, and likely frontend impact.

prompt_templates.title: Debug Authenticated Flow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced session debugging after manual login.
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect the authenticated page for console errors and failed API calls. Redact cookies, tokens, and request bodies before reporting.

prompt_templates.title: Correlate Performance Evidence
prompt_templates.prompt: Capture a page-load trace, review slow network requests, and connect the strongest evidence to concrete optimization steps.

output_examples.input: Find why the dashboard shows a blank page after login.
output: Console review found a frontend exception during dashboard rendering.
Network review found one failed session request with an authorization error.
Recommended next step: verify token refresh handling without exposing token values.

output_examples.input: Check whether the product page is slow because of API calls.
output: The slowest requests were product search and image metadata calls.
The browser trace showed rendering waited on the search response.
Recommended next step: cache metadata and defer noncritical image work.

output_examples.input: Review current browser console warnings before release.
output_examples.output: The report lists warning categories, affected pages, likely causes, and suggested owners without copying sensitive browser data.

best_practices: Use a dedicated test browser profile for debugging sessions.
Redact tokens, cookies, request bodies, and personal data before sharing output.
Start with summaries, then request full request or console details only when needed.
anti_patterns: Printing complete localStorage, sessionStorage, cookies, or authorization headers.
Leaving Chrome remote debugging available after the session ends.
Running unpinned npx packages or copied commands without review.

faq.question: What does this skill help debug?
faq.answer: It helps inspect console messages, network requests, performance traces, browser state, and authenticated web sessions.

faq.question: Does it replace browser automation tools?
faq.answer: No. It is focused on DevTools debugging, not screenshots, form filling, or broad automation workflows.

faq.question: Can it work with logged-in sessions?
faq.answer: Yes, if Chrome is already logged in and DevTools access is configured. Sensitive data must be redacted.

faq.question: Why is remote debugging a security concern?
faq.answer: A DevTools endpoint can inspect and control browser pages. Use loopback access, a test profile, and short sessions.

faq.question: What should users avoid sharing?
faq.answer: Avoid sharing cookies, tokens, authorization headers, personal data, full storage dumps, and private request bodies.

faq.question: Which AI tools are supported?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
